beliefs.practice: Do not create a new MongoClient/connection for every request; instantiate a single MongoClient at app startup and reuse it for all requests (e.g., create client in FastAPI startup event and store in app.state). Set an explicit maxPoolSize (e.g., maxPoolSize=100) appropriate to your concurrency and avoid creating many processes each making new clients.

Keep the DocumentDB connection string / credentials out of source control and out of logs; read the connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or Azure Key Vault at runtime. Do not write the actual secret into README or fixtures; provide only a .env.example placeholder.

Use TLS/SSL and lock down network access for the cluster: require TLS in the connection string (ssl=true or tls=true), restrict allowed client IP ranges, and use firewall rules or VNet integration / private endpoints rather than exposing the cluster widely.

Create explicit indexes for the fields you query with regex or equality (e.g., normalized_name, alias, country_code). For regex queries that are not left-anchored, store and index normalized/denormalized tokens (lowercased, ASCII-folded) or use an n-gram/trigram token array field and index that field instead of relying on unindexed regex.

For vector search, store embeddings in a single array field (e.g., embedding) and create a vector index with explicit algorithm and parameters (algorithm: hnsw or diskann; set dims equal to embedding length and tune m/efConstruction or nlist/ef as supported). Record the index name and algorithm parameters in code or infra so they can be recreated deterministically.

Keep metadata about embedding generation with each document (embedding_model, embedding_version, embedding_timestamp) and reject or reindex mismatched embedding versions at query time so vector searches compare compatible vectors only.

When combining vector similarity and regex/text signals, normalize each signal to a common scale before weighted aggregation; store both the raw metrics (cosine similarity, regex score) and the combined score in the screening report, and make weighting configurable rather than hard-coded.

Provision or autoscale throughput to account for vector index memory/compute costs (vector queries are expensive); test representative queries and use RU/s autoscale or higher provisioned RU for collections with vector indexes rather than leaving default low throughput.

Use explain() / query plan inspection for both regex and vector queries during development to ensure your indexes are being used; if your vector index creation tool fails, create the index via createIndexes (PyMongo) and verify plans with the cluster's tools.

Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network or 5xx errors, but ensure idempotency for retried writes (use upsert with stable IDs or idempotency tokens). Limit retries to a small number and do not retry non-idempotent multi-document transactions blindly.
Use projections to return only the fields needed for the screening response (e.g., name, source_id, similarity_score) to reduce network bandwidth and RU cost rather than returning full documents.

For fuzzy name matching, avoid expensive full-collection regex scans in production; instead either (a) maintain a text index and use text search for tokens, (b) store tokenized n-grams in an indexed array field and query those, or (c) scope regex searches with a prefilter (e.g., country or name length) to limit candidate set.

When creating indexes from code, detect and handle 'index already exists' errors and fall back to idempotent createIndexes calls. Document and log why you used a fallback (e.g., MCP helper failed) and include automated verification that the index exists post-creation.

Use collection-level or document-level TTL only for ephemeral or test data; for canonical sanctions lists do not enable TTL. If tests create data in the shared database, use a dedicated test collection or prefix and clean up after tests.

Restrict account keys and use least-privilege accounts / roles where available: use a read-only account for screening queries and a separate write/admin account for seeding and index creation; rotate credentials periodically.

Record and surface provenance for each match returned (which index matched, vector similarity value, regex pattern that matched, source id, and embedding version) so reviewers can audit why a candidate was returned.

Use consistent normalization before storing and searching names (lowercasing, removing punctuation, Unicode NFKC, ASCII folding) and store the normalized value in an indexed field rather than normalizing only at query time.

Instrument and monitor query latencies, RU consumption per operation, and index size. Capture metrics for vector search (latency, candidate counts) so you can tune index algorithm parameters (ef, m, nlist) and provisioned throughput appropriately.

When seeding data in CI/tests, run seeds against the sandbox database sample_banking_18 only and ensure cleanup or use unique collection names per test run. Do not seed or modify other databases on the cluster.

Be explicit about sort and limit for similarity queries: apply a sensible limit (e.g., top K = 50) on vector search results before applying expensive regex checks, and use a deterministic tie-breaker (e.g., _id) so results are stable across runs.
